parts.text:
{
  "extractions": [
    {
      "unit": "F001:F004",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "definition",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001"],
        "scope_text": "Applies to an employee of a covered employer under the FMLA.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": ["F002", "F003", "F004"],
        "choice_quote": "F001:F004",
        "choice_text": "All of the following three requirements must be met: (1) has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months; (2) has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave; and (3) is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.",
        "logic_quote": "F001:F004",
        "references": ["§ 825.801", "§ 825.105(b)"],
        "statement": "An eligible employee is defined as an employee of a covered employer who meets all three criteria: has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months; has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave; and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F005",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001", "F005"],
        "scope_text": "Governs the 12-month employment requirement for an employee to be eligible under the FMLA, subject to the conditions of paragraph (b).",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "need not",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F005",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, provided the conditions of paragraph (b) are met."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F006",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "exemption",
        "scope_quotes": ["F006"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2).",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "need not",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F006",
        "references": ["paragraph (b)(2)"],
        "statement": "Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2), employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F007:F009",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F007:F009"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, when an employment period precedes a break in service of more than seven years under specified conditions.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": ["F008", "F009"],
        "choice_quote": "F008:F009",
        "choice_text": "Either: (i) the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of his or her USERRA-covered service obligation; or (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.",
        "logic_quote": "F007:F009",
        "references": ["USERRA, 38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq."],
        "statement": "Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where the break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation, or where a written agreement (including a collective bargaining agreement) exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F008",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F008"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F008",
        "references": ["USERRA, 38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq."],
        "statement": "The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer, though this does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under USERRA."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F010",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F010"],
        "scope_text": "When an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F010",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including periods of paid or unpaid leave during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer, that week counts as a week of employment."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F010",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "definition",
        "scope_quotes": ["F010"],
        "scope_text": "For purposes of determining whether intermittent/occasional/casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F010",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "For purposes of determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed to be equal to 12 months."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F011",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "permission",
        "scope_quotes": ["F011"],
        "scope_text": "When determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "Nothing in this section prevents",
        "modality": "may",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F011",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Nothing in this section prevents employers from considering employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F011",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F011"],
        "scope_text": "If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F011",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years, the employer must do so uniformly with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F012",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F012"],
        "scope_text": "Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F012",
        "references": ["paragraph (c)(2)", "§ 825.801", "29 CFR part 785"],
        "statement": "Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) and § 825.801, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to the principles established under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) for determining compensable hours of work, where the determining factor is the number of hours an employee has worked for the employer within the meaning of the FLSA, without limitation by recordkeeping methods or inaccurate compensation agreements."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F012",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "permission",
        "scope_quotes": ["F012"],
        "scope_text": "For determining hours worked under FLSA principles.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "may",
        "modality": "may",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F012",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA's principles may be used."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F013",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F013"],
        "scope_text": "Applies to an employee returning from or reemployed following USERRA-covered service in determining eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave.",
        "context_quotes": ["F013"],
        "modality_quote": "shall",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F013",
        "references": ["§ 825.801(c)"],
        "statement": "An employee returning from USERRA-covered service shall be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service, which are added to hours actually worked during the previous 12-month period to meet the hours of service requirement."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F013",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F013"],
        "scope_text": "In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "generally",
        "modality": "possible",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F013",
        "references": ["§ 825.801(c)"],
        "statement": "The employee's pre-service work schedule can generally be used for calculations to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F014",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F014"],
        "scope_text": "In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including employees exempt from FLSA recordkeeping requirements.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F014",
        "references": ["29 CFR part 541", "§ 825.102", "§ 825.801(d)"],
        "statement": "In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee (including FLSA-exempt employees), the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F014",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F014"],
        "scope_text": "When an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked and claims that employees (such as full-time teachers who work outside the classroom or at home) are not eligible for FMLA leave.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F014",
        "references": ["§ 825.102", "§ 825.801(d)"],
        "statement": "An employer must be able to clearly demonstrate that the employee did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months (for example, full-time teachers of an elementary or secondary school system, institution of higher education, or other educational establishment) in order to claim that the employee is not eligible for FMLA leave."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F015",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F015"],
        "scope_text": "Governs the timing of determining whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed for a total of at least 12 months.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F015",
        "references": ["§ 825.300(b)"],
        "statement": "The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F015",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F015"],
        "scope_text": "When an employee is on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F015",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "An employee may be on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement, and in that event, any portion of the leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason after the employee meets the eligibility requirement would be FMLA leave."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F016",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F016"],
        "scope_text": "To ascertain an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits regarding whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F016",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles to ascertain an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits is determined when the employee gives notice of the need for leave."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F016",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F016"],
        "scope_text": "Once an employee is determined eligible in response to a notice of the need for leave, whether leave is taken at one time or on an intermittent or reduced leave schedule basis.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F016",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Once an employee is determined eligible in response to a notice of the need for leave (whether taken at one time or on an intermittent or reduced leave schedule basis), the employee's eligibility is not affected by any subsequent change in the number of employees employed at or within 75 miles of the worksite for that specific notice of need for leave."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F016",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "prohibition",
        "scope_quotes": ["F016"],
        "scope_text": "When an employee's leave has already started and the employee count drops below 50.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "may not",
        "modality": "must_not",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F016",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "An employer may not terminate employee leave that has already started if the employee count drops below 50."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F016",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F016"],
        "scope_text": "When an employer employs 50 or more employees (e.g., 60 in August) at the time an otherwise eligible employee gives notice of the need for leave, even if the employer expects the number to drop below 50 (e.g., to 40 in December) when the leave begins.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F016",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "An employer must grant FMLA benefits to an otherwise eligible employee who gives notice of the need for leave when 50 or more employees are employed within 75 miles, even if the employer expects the count to drop below 50 by the time the leave is scheduled to begin."
      }
    }
  ]
}

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies to an employee of a covered employer under the FMLA.
unit_attributes.choice_text: All of the following three requirements must be met: (1) has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months; (2) has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave; and (3) is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.
unit_attributes.statement: An eligible employee is defined as an employee of a covered employer who meets all three criteria: has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months; has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave; and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Governs the 12-month employment requirement for an employee to be eligible under the FMLA, subject to the conditions of paragraph (b).
unit_attributes.statement: The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, provided the conditions of paragraph (b) are met.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2).
unit_attributes.statement: Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2), employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, when an employment period precedes a break in service of more than seven years under specified conditions.
unit_attributes.choice_text: Either: (i) the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of his or her USERRA-covered service obligation; or (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.
unit_attributes.statement: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where the break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation, or where a written agreement (including a collective bargaining agreement) exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer.
unit_attributes.statement: The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer, though this does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under USERRA.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including periods of paid or unpaid leave during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer, that week counts as a week of employment.

unit_attributes.scope_text: For purposes of determining whether intermittent/occasional/casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: For purposes of determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed to be equal to 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: Nothing in this section prevents employers from considering employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.

unit_attributes.scope_text: If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years, the employer must do so uniformly with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees.
unit_attributes.statement: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) and § 825.801, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to the principles established under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) for determining compensable hours of work, where the determining factor is the number of hours an employee has worked for the employer within the meaning of the FLSA, without limitation by recordkeeping methods or inaccurate compensation agreements.

unit_attributes.scope_text: For determining hours worked under FLSA principles.
unit_attributes.statement: Any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA's principles may be used.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies to an employee returning from or reemployed following USERRA-covered service in determining eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave.
unit_attributes.statement: An employee returning from USERRA-covered service shall be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service, which are added to hours actually worked during the previous 12-month period to meet the hours of service requirement.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.statement: The employee's pre-service work schedule can generally be used for calculations to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including employees exempt from FLSA recordkeeping requirements.
unit_attributes.statement: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee (including FLSA-exempt employees), the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked and claims that employees (such as full-time teachers who work outside the classroom or at home) are not eligible for FMLA leave.
unit_attributes.statement: An employer must be able to clearly demonstrate that the employee did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months (for example, full-time teachers of an elementary or secondary school system, institution of higher education, or other educational establishment) in order to claim that the employee is not eligible for FMLA leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Governs the timing of determining whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed for a total of at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employee is on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: An employee may be on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement, and in that event, any portion of the leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason after the employee meets the eligibility requirement would be FMLA leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: To ascertain an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits regarding whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles.
unit_attributes.statement: Whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles to ascertain an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits is determined when the employee gives notice of the need for leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Once an employee is determined eligible in response to a notice of the need for leave, whether leave is taken at one time or on an intermittent or reduced leave schedule basis.
unit_attributes.statement: Once an employee is determined eligible in response to a notice of the need for leave (whether taken at one time or on an intermittent or reduced leave schedule basis), the employee's eligibility is not affected by any subsequent change in the number of employees employed at or within 75 miles of the worksite for that specific notice of need for leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employee's leave has already started and the employee count drops below 50.
unit_attributes.statement: An employer may not terminate employee leave that has already started if the employee count drops below 50.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employer employs 50 or more employees (e.g., 60 in August) at the time an otherwise eligible employee gives notice of the need for leave, even if the employer expects the number to drop below 50 (e.g., to 40 in December) when the leave begins.
unit_attributes.statement: An employer must grant FMLA benefits to an otherwise eligible employee who gives notice of the need for leave when 50 or more employees are employed within 75 miles, even if the employer expects the count to drop below 50 by the time the leave is scheduled to begin.
